paper.title_en: Energy Spectrum of Massless Klein-Gordon Field in Differentially Curved Spacetime Geometry
paper.abstract_en: This study investigates the Klein-Gordon equation with massless in the Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) gravitational framework, incorporating the effects of the Wu-Yang magnetic monopole, the Aharonov-Bohm flux, and the pseudoharmonic potential. The formulation is developed in a global monopole space-time, allowing the combined geometric, topological, and nonlinear gravitational contributions to modify the relativistic energy spectrum. Because the corresponding radial equation admits Confluent Heun series/polynomials solution, part of the energy levels that satisfy conditional exact solvability are reported. The graphical analysis shows how the parameters $\alpha$, $\sigma$, $\kappa$, $A$, and $B$ influence the spectral structure and reveal features not present in earlier models, particularly in relation to the stability of energy levels under variations of external fields and curvature deformation. Additional emphasis is placed on two parameters: the oscillator frequency $\Omega$, controlling the confinement strength, and the Aharonov-Bohm flux $\phi$, reflecting the sensitivity of the spectra to gauge-generated geometric phases. These results highlight the stabilizing role of EiBI gravity and show how nonlinear geometry and topological fields collectively shape the quantum behavior of massless scalar relativistic particles in curved space-time.
